claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is an fcc high-entropy alloy at room temperature.
The initial fcc HEA coating has high strain-hardening capacity and ductility at room temperature.
Wear resistance initially increases as ambient temperature rises.
Elevated ambient temperature thermally activates an fcc-to-hcp transition in the HEA coating.
Wear resistance degrades after the thermally activated fcc-to-hcp transition.
The high-temperature hcp phase is brittle relative to the fcc phase.
In CoCrFeMnNi, sufficiently high hydrostatic pressure produces an fcc-to-hcp polymorphic transition.
The pressure-induced hcp phase in CoCrFeMnNi can remain after decompression.
Low stacking-fault energy of approximately 20 mJ/m² facilitates the pressure-induced fcc-to-hcp transition in CoCrFeMnNi through stacking faults, dislocations, and twinning.
An as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA exhibits a room-temperature σ_UTS/σ_0.2 ratio near 16.
The extraordinary strain hardening represented by σ_UTS/σ_0.2 near 16 is an intrinsic property of the fcc phase relevant to the proposed coating.
The hcp phase lacks the stacking-fault-energy and dislocation-storage mechanisms responsible for the fcc phase's strain hardening.
Reduced work-hardening capacity after formation of hcp accelerates tribological wear.
Residual hcp regions act as stress concentrators or brittle sites during wear.
Before the critical transition, thermal softening, improved conformal contact, or dynamic recovery keeps the wear rate low or decreases it.
Above the critical temperature, the wear rate increases sharply because of fcc loss, brittle-like hcp behavior, or phase-boundary decohesion.
The ambient-pressure degradation boundary is likely between 500 and 800 K.
At high pressures of 6–26 GPa, heating retained hcp CoCrFeMnNi causes an inverse hcp-to-fcc transition, with the transition beginning near 1400 K at 26 GPa.
In CoCrFeMnNi, hcp is thermodynamically favored at lower temperatures and higher pressures, whereas fcc is favored at higher temperatures and lower pressures.
A transition-metal matrix may alter the coating's thermal phase stability or transformation kinetics.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis says increasing temperature drives fcc-to-hcp, but the mechanism and uncertainty acknowledge the cited inverse hcp-to-fcc transition on heating and the thermodynamic preference for fcc at higher temperature and lower pressure.

The boundary treats the approximately 1400 K high-pressure observation as a reference for estimating an fcc-to-hcp thermal threshold, while the uncertainty field correctly identifies that observation as an hcp-to-fcc transition.
